name: TrustPad
rootCause: Lack of msg.sender address verification. Lost: ~$155K

descriptions.text: Lack of msg.sender address verification. Lost: ~$155K

- The function receiveUpPool has no access control or msg.sender validation, as a result, it could be called by anyone to manipulate the newlockstartTime. - By repeatedly calling receiveUpPool and withdraw , the attacker could keep claiming rewards. Vulnerable code snippet: - Function receiveUpPool: Here msg.sender could be different from account Attack tx: https://explorer.phalcon.xyz/tx/bsc/0x191a34e6c0780c3d1ab5c9bc04948e231d742b7d88e0e4f85568d57fcdc03182 Analysis: https://twitter.com/BeosinAlert/status/1721800306101793188

Multi-chain launchpad platform TrustPad tweeted that one of the staking contracts was attacked. According to SlowMist's analysis, the lock time was manipulated due to obtaining an incorrect LockStartTime.

TrustPad’s LaunchpadLockableStaking contract on BNB Chain was exploited on 2023-11-06 after the receiveUpPool() migration path accepted unauthorized external calls. Public analyses and checked exploit transactions describe repeated reward-accounting manipulation that extracted roughly 615 BNB, publicly valued near $151K to $155K, before part of the proceeds moved into Tornado Cash. The LaunchpadLockableStaking contract at 0xe613c058701c768e0d04d1bf8e6a6dc1a0c6d48a reportedly failed to validate msg.sender inside receiveUpPool(). Public analyses and exploit reproductions state that arbitrary callers could manipulate staking lock timing and pending reward…

TrustPad's staking contract on BNB Chain was exploited on 6 November 2023, allowing an attacker to withdraw approximately $155,000 worth of tokens by manipulating staking reward logic. The root cause was a missing check on msg.sender in receiveUpPool, enabling unauthorized manipulation of staking state. The receiveUpPool function in TrustPad's staking contract failed to verify that the caller was authorized, allowing an attacker to invoke privileged reward manipulation operations.
